desc:
A Squarespace site management starter sprint gives busy owners a fixed round of checks, fixes and content updates. Ecom Swift LLC works through your list in your own account and sends a short report of what changed.

## What is a Squarespace site management starter sprint?

A Squarespace site management starter sprint is a fixed block of maintenance work done once, for a set scope, with no ongoing contract. We check the site, repair what is broken and then complete the updates you have been putting off: text, photos, products, blog posts, events, forms and newsletter blocks.

Monthly care can be discussed separately, and nothing renews without your written agreement.

## Why a site needs regular attention

A site that is not looked after slowly goes stale. Opening hours are wrong, an event from last season still sits on the home page, a product shows as available when it is not, and a form link points nowhere. Visitors judge the business by these details, and search engines favor sites that stay current.

Owners rarely lack the skill to fix these things. They lack the time. One focused session works through the whole pile of small jobs together.

## How upkeep affects enquiries and customer trust

Fresh content tells visitors the business is open and active. Accurate prices and stock levels prevent disappointment at checkout. Working forms and links mean a prospect who tries to contact you actually reaches you.

Resized images shorten loading time, which matters most on phones. Reviewing page titles on key pages helps each page describe itself in search results. These changes are small, yet they remove friction that quietly costs enquiries.

## What a good maintenance round covers

- A site check that lists broken links, missing images and outdated text.
- Content updates to pages, with wording supplied by you.
- Product edits such as prices, descriptions, variants and stock.
- Blog posts and event listings formatted and published.
- Forms and newsletter blocks tested with a real entry.
- Large photos resized to load faster.
- Small layout fixes where something has slipped out of place.
- A look at your plan, domain and extensions for anything that needs attention.
- A plan for the following month, in the larger package.

## What we do

We begin with a site check and write the fix list. Then we work through your update list in priority order, publishing only what you have approved. At the end you receive a short summary of every change, so you know exactly what was touched.

The Basic package pairs the site check with a handful of content updates. Standard adds more updates, plus blog or product edits, a newsletter check and image resizing. Premium covers a full sprint with design improvements, a page title review and a plan for the next month.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Send your update list in one message, in order of importance.
- Supply final wording, prices and photos.
- Tell us which changes need to go live on a particular date.
- Keep a record of your plan, domain and renewal dates.

**Avoid:**
- Sending half-written text.
- Asking for a redesign inside a maintenance sprint.
- Expecting us to answer customers or manage orders, which stays with you.
- Leaving old announcements online after they expire.

## Who this is for

A shop owner who has not touched the site since a busy season wants it brought up to date. A speaker or trainer with new dates, photos and a blog post to publish needs them live quickly. A founder who has just taken over a site wants to know what state it is in and have the first fixes done.

## How to get started

Send your site address and your list of updates. We never need your password, and the work stays inside your own account. Invite us as a contributor with the permissions needed for content, products and settings, and remove the invitation when the sprint ends. If we find something outside the scope, such as moving to another plan or domain, we tell you before changing anything.
